# 0065: A subagent is priced at its own model's rates, from the final usage of each call

Status: accepted, 2026-10-08.
Refines [0033](0033-subagent-transcripts-are-captured-and-billed.md) (subagent transcripts are captured and billed) with which rates bill them.
Refines [0051](0051-long-context-is-a-tier-priced-per-call-and-records-are-curated.md) (each call is priced on its own) with which row a call is priced from.

## Context

Claude's CLI reports a session's whole cost, subagents included.
For the 82 claude sessions without subagents, the plugin's estimate matched it to the cent.
For the 57 with subagents it drifted from -23% to +25%.
That made the delegation treatment look more expensive than it was: up to 87% on a codex parent.

Two causes, both visible in the captured logs.
Every call of a run was priced at the run's model, so a Haiku subagent under an Opus parent was billed as Opus.
The model that answered is named on each record of the subagent's own transcript.

And a subagent transcript streams a call's usage across that call's records.
One call recorded output tokens of 4, 4, 4 and then 917, while the main session's log repeats the final figure on every record.
The ledger kept the first, so subagent output was undercounted about 100-fold.

## Decision

**A subagent records the model that answered it.** Claude's is the model its assistant records name.
Codex's is its rollout's last `turn_context`, because a fork first replays its parent's.

**Each part of a run is priced at its own model's rates.** The primary's calls bill at the run's model, and each subagent's at its own.
A subagent whose transcript names no model bills at its parent's, the only rate it can be shown to have.
A subagent model with no price row stops pricing, as an unpriced run does (ADR 0007); it never borrows a neighbour's rate.

**The parts are summed before any rounding.** So a run priced in parts costs the same, to the micro-dollar, as one priced whole.
Each subagent also carries its own `estimated_cost_usd`.
The run's `rates_applied` stays the primary's row, the one a reader checks it against.

**A call bills its final usage.** When one message spans several records, the ledger keeps the furthest-along usage, not the first.

## Consequences

Replayed against the cache, all 139 claude sessions now land within 0.5% of the CLI's own cost.
The 57 with subagents sum to $52.41, exactly the CLI's figure; the worst single session is 0.26% off.
The comparison is the check this record leaves behind, and a replay re-runs it for free.

Codex prints no cost of its own, so its subagents are priced by the same rule but cannot be cross-checked the same way.

The characterization goldens gain each subagent's `model` and `estimated_cost_usd`, and no total moves.

## Lens

A cost estimate is only trustworthy where it can be checked against the provider's own bill, and it must be checked there.
Price each call at the rates of the model that answered it, and count what it produced, not the first fragment of it.
